subject: Deployment mode tradeoffs, region constraints & MAP goalposts
messages:
From: Samuel Park <sam@orchidhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22 09:04 PDT
Subject: Quick q: deployment modes and timeline for evaluation

Hi Irene,

We're scoping an evaluation MAP for Orchid Health and want to lock the deployment-mode decision early so our security and procurement teams can start parallel checks. High-level constraints: all PHI must remain in US regions; we prefer a single-region deployment for latency predictability; target evaluation window is June 1 - June 30 with a commercial decision by mid-June.

Question: from a practical standpoint what configurations force us toward Dedicated or Private vs Hosted? Also, what does a typical MAP look like to get from POC to an initial production pilot in 4-6 weeks?

Thanks,
Sam
Senior Product Manager
Orchid Health

-----

On Tue, May 22, 2026 at 11:20 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick q: deployment modes and timeline for evaluation

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear constraints. Short answer up front: Hosted can work for evaluation if you accept a redwood-hosted US region with customer-supplied encryption keys (KMS) and a contractual data residency clause; Dedicated is the usual recommendation when you need predictable tail-latency, capacity isolation, and customer-dedicated GPU pools; Private (VPC/on-prem) is required when procurement/legal require customer-managed networking or air-gapped environments.

Proposed MAP (high level) to hit a mid-June decision:
- Week of May 25: technical scoping workshop (security, infra, product) — 90 minutes.
- May 27–June 3: evaluation kit & test dataset ingestion, baseline perf runs in hosted (or dedicated trial if requested).
- June 4–11: quality regressions and integration smoke tests.
- June 12–16: exec review, pricing/terms negotiation, procurement checklist.
- Target commercial decision: June 15–18.

Can we schedule the workshop Wed May 27 at 10am PT? I'll loop in Markus (solutions) for the infra tradeoffs and Ben (sales engineering) for pricing examples. I'll attach an initial MAP workbook and a short data flow diagram.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

I've sketched the infra tradeoffs after a quick pass on their constraints. Notes below — copying the diagram reference (data_flow_diagram.pdf).

- Hosted (redwood-managed in a US region): fastest to start (hours to provision), supports customer-managed KMS for at-rest keys and TLS for transit. Good for evaluations where the data set is a representative sample and legal can sign a limited-data residency addendum. Downsides: shared GPU pools mean noisy neighbors at extreme tail loads; no dedicated SLAs for latency unless moved to Dedicated.
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools in our region): provides capacity isolation, predictable P99 latency, and optional VPC peering. Typical lead-time: 1–2 weeks to reserve capacity if we have slot availability; for short evaluations we can do a reserved trial for the MAP. Recommended when the evaluation will use larger real datasets or stress tests that risk interfering with other tenants.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): requires procurement + network setup, IP allowlists, and (if on-prem) physical install. Lead-time 4–8+ weeks depending on infra approvals. Use only if procurement/legal refuse hosted/dedicated or require air-gapped ops.

Performance guardrails for the MAP:
- For latency-sensitive endpoints (sub-150ms tail target), prefer Dedicated or smaller-seq-length model variants on Hosted.
- For throughput/scale tests, benchmark on Dedicated.
- KV prefix caching and continuous batching recommendations will be included in the MAP workbook.

I've attached a stub SOC2 evidence pack and the data flow diagram to pass to their security reviewer.

Attachments: data_flow_diagram.pdf, soc2_evidence_stub.pdf

-Markus
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Quick pricing note for the MAP:
- Hosted evaluation (redwood-managed): per-token consumption + temporary evaluation credits. Lower upfront, faster to start.
- Dedicated trial: monthly reserved capacity pro-rated; we typically offer a short-term concession for evaluation (one-time trial credit) to mimic production performance.
- Private: pricing includes platform license + ops support; higher upfront and longer procurement path.

Recommendation: Start in Hosted with customer KMS and strict ingestion rules for the June eval window. If performance or tail-latency becomes an issue during the first week we can spin a Dedicated trial (we have limited slots in us-west). This minimizes procurement friction and keeps their target decision date intact.

Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
